description.en: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai was a first-century Jewish leader and scholar who oversaw the fragile transition of the Jewish people to life without a [Temple](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/beit-hamikdash?sort=Relevance&tab=notable-sources), upon the destruction of the Second Temple in 70 CE at the hands of the Romans. While he sought accommodation with the Romans, he was unable to convince the faction of zealots to give up their position, which ultimately led to the destruction of [Jerusalem](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/jerusalem?tab=admin). Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai's students smuggled him out of Jerusalem, enabling him to renew Jewish life and learning from [Yavneh](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/yavneh?tab=admin). He is famous for establishing  *takkanot*, halakhic decrees, that represent the shift from a Temple-centric Judaism to a Judaism without a Temple.
description.he: רבן יוחנן היה תנא ומנהיג בולט שניהל את המעבר הרגיש של העם היהודי למציאות שאחרי חורבן בית המקדש. בתור נשיא הוא ניהל משא ומתן עם הרומאים אבל לא הצליח לשכנע את הקנאים, וכשל זה הוביל לחורבן ירושלים. רבן יוחנן נמלט מן החורבן ובנה מחדש את החיים היהודיים ביבנה, ובכלל זה תיקן תקנות זכר למקדש.

en.title: A New Approach to Timekeeping
en.prompt: Before the advent of an established Jewish calendar, new months would be declared following the testimony of witnesses who saw the new moon. en.ai_prompt: The decree to accept testimony for the new month throughout the entire day marked a pivotal adaptation of Jewish law after the Temple's destruction. The Mishnah, the first codification of Jewish law from the early third-century land of Israel, records enactments that were crucial for maintaining Jewish religious practices in the absence of the Temple.

en.title: Redefining Jewish Worship and Leadership
en.prompt: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai and the sages of Yavneh redefined Jewish worship and leadership, ensuring Jewish survival and adaptability after the destruction of the Second Temple. This contemporary text explores the innovative spirit of the Yavneh generation.
en.ai_context: contemporary israeli halakhic work commenting on the influence ben zakkai had on worship
en.ai_prompt: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai and the Sages of Yavne redefined Jewish worship and leadership, ensuring Jewish survival and adaptability after the destruction of the Second Temple. This text explores the innovative spirit of the Yavne generation, which shifted Judaism from a Temple-centric practice to one that could thrive in any location and time.
